message.content:
The sea typically looks **blue**—the same reason our sky does. Sunlight contains all colors, but water absorbs longer wavelengths (reds, oranges) more efficiently than shorter ones (blues, greens). As a result, when you look into clear ocean water, most of what reaches your eyes is scattered short‑wave light, giving the surface its characteristic azure hue.

Of course, the exact shade changes:

| Factor | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Depth | Deeper waters appear darker because less light penetrates. |
| Clarity / Algae | Greenish tint from phytoplankton or murkier brown/green hues near shorelines. |
| Weather & Time of Day | Warm glows during sunrise/sunset, bright turquoise under midday sun. |
| Reflection | Waves reflect surrounding skies, adding blues or even pinks/turquoise. |

So while “sea” often conjures images of deep cobalt or teal, the real world offers a spectrum influenced by natural conditions.
